evidence: io.lisp:2173-2176: `(handler-case (fnn-flock fd (logior (if exclusive +fnn-lock-ex+ +fnn-lock-sh+) +fnn-lock-nb+)) (fnn-os-error () (fnn-close fd) (fnn-refuse "store is already locked")))`. Compare fnn-store-owner-observation (io.lisp:2194-2195), which does tell EWOULDBLOCK apart from other errnos: `(if (= (fnn-os-errno e) sb-posix:ewouldblock) :held :unknown)`.
fix: Refuse "already locked" only for EWOULDBLOCK/EAGAIN. Retry EINTR. Raise any other errno as a named fault or OS error that carries its errno.
reviewer: io.lisp:2173-2176 maps any fnn-os-error from the non-blocking flock to fnn-refuse "store is already locked". fnn-store-owner-observation (io.lisp:2194-2195) does tell EWOULDBLOCK apart from other errnos. ENOLCK or EOPNOTSUPP on an odd filesystem is reported as contention (exit 1) instead of a fault. It needs an unusual mount to happen, so it is a diagnostic and classification defect.
scenario: The store is on a filesystem where flock fails with ENOLCK or EOPNOTSUPP (some NFS or FUSE mounts), or fails with EINTR or EBADF. fnn-acquire refuses (exit 1) with "store is already locked", and the operator goes looking for an owner that does not exist. A host or platform fault is reported as a contention refusal, so two different outcomes become one.
title: Any flock failure on the writer lock is reported as "store is already locked"
